_comment: MCU_hart: the SINGLE-HART signoff vehicle, 2026-08-24. It exists because LVS has never MATCHed at the MCU or chip level, and a 5-hart assembly is the wrong thing to debug that on. The shape is deliberately the SMALLEST assembly that still contains everything the failing signoff has to explain: one hardened hart_tile macro, the shared fabric it masters, the memory macros, the pad ring, and the AFE stub bank. Prove it with: tools/bin/bazel test //platform/common:mcu_hart_generation_test //opensource_sim/mcu_hart:all ; regenerate it with: make -C platform/common generate CONFIG=config/mcu_hart.json (and then plain make chip, to put out/ and the tracked resolved config back to Castalia).
_chipNameNote: chipName is DOCUMENTATION AND FILE-HEADER ONLY -- it does not reach an entity name. The emitted top is `entity MCU` in every configuration (Castalia, PentaWound, Argus and this one all emit it), because the entity name is fixed template text in hdl_templates/MCU.template.vhd and the whole physical flow is wired to it. So the physical agent consumes out/hdl/MCU.vhd with the top cell still called MCU; MCU_hart is what the TRM title page, the generated file headers and implementations/asic/mcu_hart/ are named.
_orchestratorNote: FALSE, and this is the load-bearing decision in the file rather than a default inherited by accident (the R-DK3 inheritance trap: orchestrator=true has been the SHIPPED DEFAULT since CPR8, so leaving this out would have selected the other arm). THE REASON IS THE VEHICLE'S SUBJECT. With orchestrator=true, hart 0 is emitted as `entity work.orch_tile`, the SOFT centre-band core -- and at numHarts=1 there are no harts 1..N-1, so the design would contain NO hart_tile instance at all. The hardened tile macro and its macro-to-top boundary are exactly what an MCU-level LVS has to reconcile, so a vehicle without one would prove the wrong thing. orchestrator=false makes hart 0 an ordinary hart_tile, and the assembly is then one hardened tile plus the always-on fabric: the failing hierarchy, minus four copies. THREE FURTHER CONSEQUENCES, all in the same direction: (1) the memory map stays v1, SH_AW=15 rather than the v2 max(derived,16), so the arbiter, the master slices and every slave decode are one address bit narrower; (2) there are no TCM apertures -- at N=1 the aperture fabric would be a read-only window through which hart 0 reaches its own TCM, pure area for no function; (3) extended flash stays at 0x20000 instead of moving to the v2 complement 0x40000, which is where the boot ROM and the XIP software already expect it. NOTE what does NOT differ: pwr_ctrl sees NHARTS=1 in either shape, because the gateable rows are 1..N-1 and that range is empty either way.
_minimalTilesNote: FALSE, pinned, and the pin is about honesty rather than hardware. MEASURED in the generator: isa.minimalTiles feeds ChipGenerator.MINIMAL_TILES, whose ONLY consumers are the three MemoryMap.vhd constants TILE_ENABLE_MUL / TILE_ENABLE_DIV / TILE_ENABLE_BITMANIP, and those constants are read ONLY by the hart_tile instances the tile loop emits for harts 1..N-1. At numHarts=1 that loop emits nothing, so the knob is RTL-INERT here in both positions -- the emitted MCU.vhd is byte-identical either way, and hart 0 takes the full CORE_ENABLE_* set regardless. What it still moves is the manual and the three dead constants. Left at its default true, this chip's MemoryMap.vhd would declare a reduced tile ISA that no hart on it has, and the TRM would describe an asymmetry between hart 0 and tiles that do not exist. false makes TILE_ENABLE_* equal CORE_ENABLE_* and the chip symmetric, which is what a one-hart chip is.
_peripheralsNote: MINIMAL, with ONE deliberate exception. Dropped: the NPU and its 16 KiB staging RAM (the largest single block on the die and nothing to do with the fabric under test), NFC0, and the four SECOND instances i2c1/uart1/spi1/timer1 -- each of those is a duplicate of a block the vehicle still carries as instance 0, so dropping them removes area without removing a single distinct cell type from the LVS problem. fieldPower is off because it is pad-side wiring only: the PWRCTRL boot-gate registers and pgood_rstn exist in the RTL unconditionally, so false ties the pad inputs and leaves the feature a provable no-op. KEPT, AGAINST THE MINIMISING INSTINCT: peripherals.cqAfeStubs. The Castalia golden master has it true and the hardened PentaWound cut has it false, and that divergence is an OPEN issue -- which means the AFE/EIS stub bank is the one block on this chip whose physical status is unknown. A signoff vehicle that omits the block nobody has closed out would prove less than it appears to, so this chip carries all five afe_stub instances (AFE0-3 in page-0 slot 12 sub-slots, EIS at 0x7C00) and they cost five 16-word register files. At numHarts=1 their OWNER_HART literals stay 0/1/2/3 as in the non-orchestrator shape: harts 1-3 do not exist, so those three sites answer to hart 0 alone through the `or hart 0' half of the ownership gate, which is behaviourally exactly what a one-hart chip should do and needs no generator special case.
_debugNote: FALSE, and this is the second inherited-default pin in the file: debug.enable became the SHIPPED DEFAULT on 2026-08-16. Debug costs this vehicle a Debug Module, a JTAG DTM, five bonded TAP balls and -- the part that matters here -- ONE MORE ARBITER MASTER, which widens the fabric from a genuinely single-master bus to two masters and defeats the point of the cut. It also forces the package: _checkDebugTransportBonded refuses to ship an on-die TAP that no pin reaches, so a debug-ON build could not wear the QFN-44 this row picks. The DM is proven at N=5 by config/castalia_debug.json and at N=18 by config/argus_debug.json; it is not this row's job.
_packageNote: The SMALLEST pinout the generator models, which is the right pad ring for the smallest die. It is also the third inherited-default pin: castalia-lqfp100 has been the default since 2026-08-16 and would put a 100-pin ring around a one-hart chip. Two side effects, both wanted: the QFN-44 bonds no JTAG TAP, which agrees with debug.enable=false above; and it bonds no electrode group, so the AFE/EIS chapter and the AfeSystemDiagram stay off. That figure ASSERTS the five-hart orchestrator shape by name and would fail the build outright on a one-hart chip -- the stub bank is still instantiated in the RTL (see the peripherals note), it is only the analog CHAPTER that the pad ring gates.
_memoryNote: memory.* is left entirely at the shipped defaults, on purpose: romSize 8192 matches the rom2k_hvt_pg macro that MCU.vhd's concurrent assert binds RomAddrBits to, and tcmSizePerHart 8192 matches the sram1p8k_hvt_pg that hart_tile.vhd:876 asserts RamSize against. Both asserts EXECUTE in //opensource_sim/mcu_hart:mcu_hart_elaborate, so a drift between this file and either macro fails a test rather than shipping a map the arrays do not honour. The Argus rows are the cautionary case: they ask for a 16 KiB TCM and no longer elaborate.
